endpoints.title: Classical Riemann hypothesis
endpoints.name: riemannHypothesis
endpoints.statement: Every nontrivial zeta zero distinct from the pole has real part one half.
premises: The Riemann zeta function vanishes at the complex number s.
The point s is neither a negative even integer nor 1.
endpoints.premiseScope: These hypotheses occur inside the stated proposition. The submitted theorem has no outer premises.
endpoints.proposition:
def RiemannZetaZerosOnLine : Prop :=
  ∀ s : ℂ, riemannZeta s = 0 → (¬∃ n : ℕ, s = -2 * ((n : ℂ) + 1)) → s ≠ 1 → s.re = 1 / 2

endpoints.title: Nonvanishing right of one half
endpoints.name: LFunction_ne_zero_of_half_lt_re
endpoints.statement: For all positive moduli and all characters, L(s,χ) is nonzero for Re(s)>1/2, excluding the principal pole.
premises: The modulus N is positive and χ is a Dirichlet character modulo N.
The real part of s exceeds one half.
Either χ is nonprincipal or s differs from 1.

endpoints.title: Dirichlet GRH in the open strip
endpoints.name: LFunction_eq_zero_re
endpoints.statement: For every character of positive modulus, any zero with 0<Re(s)<1 satisfies Re(s)=1/2.
premises: The modulus N is positive and χ is a Dirichlet character modulo N.
The real part of s is strictly between zero and one.
The Dirichlet L-function of χ vanishes at s.

components.title: The five endpoints
components.description: Ordinary RH in Mathlib's own formulation, and Dirichlet GRH for every character of every positive modulus.
components.kernel: The five named endpoint declarations were checked in the recorded full-export kernel replays.

components.title: Reflection
components.description: A zero left of the critical line reflects to a zero right of it, so the right half-plane is all one has to clear.
components.kernel: Selected declarations in this component received kernel checks at the submission pin.

components.title: Conductor descent
components.description: An imprimitive character differs from its primitive inducing character by finitely many Euler factors, none of which vanishes for $\operatorname{Re}s>0$.
components.kernel: Selected declarations in this component received kernel checks at the submission pin.

components.title: The centered prime sum
components.description: A ramp-weighted von Mangoldt sum, centered so that the main terms cancel exactly, and its positive combinations over a cyclic family of characters.
components.kernel: Selected declarations in this component received kernel checks at the submission pin.

components.title: Mellin transform and positive residues
components.description: The Mellin transform of a ramp is $n^{-s}/(s(s-1))$; a zero of any family member becomes a pole whose residue cannot be cancelled, because the weights are positive.
components.kernel: Selected declarations in this component received kernel checks at the submission pin.

components.title: The window criterion
components.description: If a positive family's prime sum stays below $Cy^\theta$ throughout arbitrarily late windows $[Y,Y^{1+\delta}]$, none of its $L$-functions vanishes to the right of $\theta$.
components.kernel: Two independent kernels checked the selected result in this component.

components.title: The order of choices
components.description: The loss exponents are fixed first; given a zero with $\beta>\tfrac12$ choose $\theta\in(\tfrac12,\beta)$, then $\varepsilon$ with $\tfrac12+9\varepsilon\le\theta$. No bound at $\varepsilon=0$ is ever needed.
components.kernel: Selected declarations in this component received kernel checks at the submission pin.

components.title: The finite character comparison
components.description: Finite Fourier orthogonality on a subgroup and an exact main-term identity convert a geometric discrepancy bound into the prime-sum bound, with exponent $\tfrac12+(e_D+e_L+7)\varepsilon$.
components.kernel: Selected declarations in this component received kernel checks at the submission pin.

components.title: The geometric family and the theta chain
components.description: A chain of about $\sqrt x$ theta lifts, with divisibility, slope and covolume control, is chosen so that both loss exponents are fixed numbers: $e_D=2$, $e_L=0$.
components.kernel: Kernel checks cover selected landmarks in this component. Other passages have a source reading.

components.title: Hosts for every character
components.description: For each primitive character $\psi$, the cohomological window produces arithmetic hosts of width $3/2$ at all large scales of a system of scales.
components.kernel: Selected declarations in this component received kernel checks at the submission pin.

components.title: The cohomological window
components.description: On a whole interval $[Y,Y^2]$, weighted lengths of locally trivial Galois cohomology of twisted modules are at most $\sqrt{\exp(x^{\varepsilon})}$, uniformly over the relevant fields.
components.kernel: Kernel checks cover selected landmarks in this component. Other passages have a source reading.

components.title: Auxiliary primes and Behrend towers
components.description: Two auxiliary primes with prescribed congruences and square-root prime-sum bounds for their quadratic twists, and an additive-combinatorial (Behrend) choice of the tower.
components.kernel: Selected declarations in this component received kernel checks at the submission pin.

components.title: The Galois row
components.description: For regular algebraic polarized cuspidal $\pi$ on $\mathrm{GL}_a$ over a CM field, a continuous semisimple $\ell$-adic representation whose Frobenius polynomials match the Satake parameters of $\pi$.
components.kernel: The component has a source reading. Its separate kernel replay is unrecorded.

components.title: Seven inputs at the decisive call
components.description: Unitary-group and local theta packages, agreement of theta integrals, local matching, a covolume bound, local Langlands parameters and the window: the seven arguments of the arithmetic theorem.
